newsitem.title: USA: IMM currency futures close dull trade barely mixed.
newsitem.headline: IMM currency futures close dull trade barely mixed.

text.p: IMM currency futures finished a session of low-volume, post-holiday trading barely mixed.
Most units registered little daily change after drifting inside tight ranges in thin trade that magnified price moves.

Yen slipped to moderate losses, with March futures setting a new contract low, this at $0.008797, in early pit trading after the U.S. dollar had hurdled the 115.00 spot level overnight for the first time in more than 3-1/2 years.
The yen succumbed partly to the sell-off in Japan's Nikkei 225 index, which fell as much as 700 points overnight and punched below 19,000 for the first time in more than a year.
The Nikkei index in Tokyo trading recouped the bulk of its losses, but still ended off 257.83 points at 19,291.58.
Several comments Thursday by Japanese government officials about the yen and Nikkei slides helped cushion the yen's drop by making traders leery of selling the unit more aggressively.
"We spent a lot of time around the 108-110 level...and now we're near 115, so maybe we're in a new range and they're (Japanese officials) getting a little worried," said one floor broker of the yen.
A Bank of Japan senior official said the central bank was carefully monitoring developments in foreign exchange markets.
A senior Ministry of Finance official said Japan's monetary authorities do not welcome "wild fluctuations in exchange rates" and that MoF is closely watching developments.
The Economic Planning Agency's vice minister Shimpei Nukaya said current Japanese economic conditions were "fairly strong" and he hoped markets would note that.
Traders also wondered about the effect of year-end plays on currencies as well, with evening of positions seen as possibly responsible for some of the yen's drop.
With several key trading centers still shuttered for Christmas holidays, futures order flows stayed very thin.
Futures volume on the price boards at the close was estimated at roughly 3,500 marks, 2,900 Swiss francs, 5,100 yen and 1,900 stg in the March contracts.
On Friday, weekly U.S. jobless claims are seen off 5,000 at 346,000 from original 351,000 reported the prior week.

November durable goods orders are seen firming 0.1 percent, but losing 0.5 percent excluding defense. March yen fell $0.000038 to $0.008803, mark rose $0.0011 to $0.6465, Swiss fr rose $0.0009 to $0.7493, pound off $0.0006 at $1.6700, Can dollar rose $0.0009 to $0.7376, Aussie dollar lost $0.0027 to $0.7940, Mex peso fell $0.000025 to $0.121725.
